Los agentes de IA podrían usarse para detectar y ejecutar ese mantenimiento invisible de forma continua, pero el cluster no aporta evidencia al respecto.

critic.argument: The claim is essentially a paraphrase of an RSS item's title, not a finding. It explicitly concedes there is no body, no data, no examples, no metrics — only a title and header string. The 'invisible technical debt' thesis is read into a title by lexical association ('Fix Like No One's Watching' → unseen work → invisible debt), which is precisely a lexical coincidence dressed as interpretation. There is nothing to corroborate; corroboration=0.50 and novelty=0.00 signal an ingestion artifact, and the brief's actual themes (AI agents, technical leadership of small teams, estimation, sequencing, teaching) are admittedly unaddressed — the author admits 'the connection is plausible but not evidenced.' Plausibility of a title is not evidence of a thesis. The claim is self-undermining: it describes the artifact accurately and then still asserts a thesis it has already shown is unsupported. The already-low stated confidence (0.15) is itself generous; nothing here survives as a substantive finding.
